data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's argument that safety is vacuous relies entirely on properties of the *replay* path — no concurrency, no interleaving, no observable intermediate states during reconstruction. But the problem asks what the log must require 'of its writers to survive at-least-once delivery,' which concerns the live delivery path where writers retry, not the replay path. A writer retrying an append in a live system that is concurrently serving reads or processing other writes does face observable intermediate states. SRC_001's mechanism conflates replay-time guarantees (which the log's total order provides) with delivery-time requirements (which writers must satisfy). The total order of the log ensures deterministic replay, but it does not eliminate concurrency during the live write/retry path. SRC_001's own countercondition #2 concedes that external side effects during retry make idempotency insufficient, yet the main claim never reconciles this with the problem's explicit focus on what *writers* must guarantee.
